newsitem.title: USA: CSCE plans flexible options on world sugar futures.
newsitem.headline: CSCE plans flexible options on world sugar futures.

text.p: The Coffee, Sugar and Cocoa Exchange plans to introduce new flexible options on its Sugar No. 11 futures contract on September 10, 1997, the CSCE said on Tuesday.
In addition, the CSCE said it plans to launch flexible options on its coffee and cocoa futures contracts by the end of the year.

The new sugar options contract, which is subject to the approval of the U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission, would allow market participants to alter several elements of a standard sugar option to broaden and customize trades.

"With this new trading tool, market participants will be able to implement strategies similar to those available in the over-the-counter market, while at the same time trading in a competitive open environment and enjoying all the other advantages and protective benefits of an exchange-traded contract," CSCE President James Bowe said in a statement.

Under the terms of the new contract, traders will be able to customize the strike price, the expiration date, the exercise style (American or European) and the way in which the strike price is specified. European-style options can only be exercised on expiration day, while American-style options can be exercised on any business day until expiration day.

The options will be introduced as a quote-on-request market. Other contract terms are the same as those of a standard futures options contract. ((-- W Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
